title: On Forgiving the debt after many years
subtitle: 品格修养 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 品格修养（人与自我·做人与做事·优秀品行与道德品质）
meta: 主题语境：品格修养（人与自我·做人与做事·优秀品行与道德品质）　|　核心词汇：forgive　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 forgive 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1978 the shopkeeper ① forgave the debt after many years before dawn, and every buyer in the shop said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three months on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the shopkeeper ② forgives the debt after many years in public without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ forgive the debt after many years at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ forgiven the debt after many years before — a line in the account for July 1972 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Forgiving the debt after many years before dawn, the shopkeeper said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the scale at the far counter, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ forgive him the whole sum at last in public, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Forgive him the whole sum at last at once and never mention it again.

By 1985 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the account, and a new buyer from the next shop ⑧ forgives him the whole sum at last before dawn every month without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the counter, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ forgave the debt after many years again when nobody else would.

⑩ To forgive the debt after many years, my mother said in 1990, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the shop remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the shop forgets, somebody forgives the debt after many years in public again and somebody must forgive the debt after many years before dawn all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 原谅（一般过去式 forgave the debt after many years：1978 年掌柜头一回这样做，天没亮就）
B. v. 原谅（一般现在 forgives the debt after many years：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 原谅（不定式 to forgive the debt after many years：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 原谅（过去完成时 had forgiven the debt after many years：1972 年七月的账本上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 原谅（动名词 forgiving the debt after many years 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 免除（forgive him the whole sum at last：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去免除终于把整笔款项都免了）
G. v. 免除（forgive him the whole sum at last：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 原谅（后段两处：新来的买主照例 forgives him the whole sum at last，而母亲又一次 forgave the debt after many years）

answers.why: forgive 意为“原谅”，1978 年掌柜天没亮就原谅多年之后免了那笔账，那是铺子里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 forgave。
forgive 意为“原谅”，自那以后掌柜当着众人面把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 forgives。
forgive 意为“原谅”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯原谅多年之后免了那笔账”，此处为不定式 to forgive the debt after many years。
forgive 意为“原谅”，账本里 七月 那行字说明早在 1985 年之前就有人原谅过，故用过去完成时 had forgiven。
forgive 意为“原谅”，掌柜说“原谅多年之后免了那笔账这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 forgiving the debt after many years 作主语。
forgive 意为“免除”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去免除终于把整笔款项都免了”，should ever 之后用原形 forgive him the whole sum at last。
forgive 意为“免除”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻免除终于把整笔款项都免了（forgive him the whole sum at last at once），以后再也不要提起。
forgive 意为“原谅”，新来的买主每个月份都照例免除终于把整笔款项都免了，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 forgives。
forgive 意为“原谅”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次天没亮就原谅多年之后免了那笔账，用一般过去式 forgave 叙述。
forgive 意为“原谅”，结尾那句是母亲 1990 年的话：要原谅多年之后免了那笔账，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和铺子记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 forgive 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1978 the shopkeeper forgave the debt after many years before dawn, and nobody in the shop forgot it.
Even now the shopkeeper forgives the debt after many years in public whenever the shop asks.
Forgiving the debt after many years before dawn, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever forgive him the whole sum at last in public, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new buyer from the next shop forgives him the whole sum at last before dawn every month, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother forgave the debt after many years again, and the shop remembered that half.
